input.rationale: Built and ran the two focused probes registered last turn in one harness (assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, reusing the repo's own test helpers newTestConfig/newTestMemoryStorage/withPeers/newNetwork/readMessages). Local construction feedback only, no retained receipt yet, so the experiments request below asks the controller to run the same fixed harness in isolation. Observations (draft-side run, CA_EVENT lines): (1) campaign guard - a voter whose log has entry 2 as EntryConfChangeV2 at term 1 with HardState.Commit=2 and Config.Applied=1 reports applied=1, committed=2, promotable=true, has_unapplied=true; MsgHup on it leaves state=StateFollower, term=1, msgs=0 and MsgTimeoutNow (carrying the term) likewise leaves state=StateFollower, msgs=0; after the application catches up (raftLog.appliedTo(2,0)) has_unapplied=false and MsgHup turns it into StateCandidate at term 2 with vote=self and MsgVote to voters [2,3]; the control with a normal entry at index 2 and the same applied=1/committed=2 gap reports has_unapplied=false and campaigns immediately (StateCandidate, term 2, MsgVote to [2,3]). So the discriminator resolves toward the source reading: suppression is keyed on the entry type in (applied, committed], blocks both the time-based and the leadership-transfer paths, and ends as soon as raft's applied index covers the entry. (2) ReadIndex across a term change - a leader (term 1, committed=2, committed_entry_in_term=true) admits a read (unconfirmed_reads=1, read_states=0, admission commit=2); a real peer campaign at term 2 makes it a follower and the admitted request is dropped with no completion (read_states=0, ctx_A_completed=false, unconfirmed_reads=0, confirmed_reads=0), while a read admitted afterwards on the new leader is confirmed by one peer heartbeat response echoing the leader's context and delivered with index=3 equal to the commit index at admission. Neither observation yields a defect under the stated conditions: the campaign suppression is the documented safety intent (campaign with an applied configuration), and the dropped read is the lossiness the Node.ReadIndex contract already places on the caller ('request can be lost without notice, therefore it is user's job to ensure read index retries'). I therefore assert no defect for either question, and request the formal receipt so the negative is evidence-backed rather than source-only.

scope.description: One fixed harness with two sourced probes. Probe A (TestAssuranceCampaignWithUnappliedConfChange) covers the campaign admission guard: a voter built from MemoryStorage with entries [1]=normal and [2]=EntryConfChangeV2 at term 1, HardState.Commit=2 and Config.Applied=1, driven by MsgHup and by MsgTimeoutNow (term-carrying), then re-driven after raftLog.appliedTo(2,0); a control node has the same applied/committed gap but a normal entry at index 2. Probe B (TestAssuranceReadIndexAcrossTermChange) covers ReadOnlySafe completion across an authority change: elect a leader over a real 3-node in-process network, commit an entry in its term, admit a MsgReadIndex with no heartbeat responses delivered, then deliver a real higher-term campaign message from peer 2, and finally confirm a read admitted on the new leader with a single peer heartbeat response echoing the leader's context. Each case prints one CA_EVENT JSON line with the observed operands (state, term, vote, applied, committed, has_unapplied, unconfirmed_reads, confirmed_reads, read_states, vote targets, read index).
assumptions: Both probes use the snapshot's own test facilities (newTestRaft/newTestConfig/newTestMemoryStorage/withPeers/newNetwork) in one process.
Probe A's supplied state is a real MemoryStorage prefix plus a HardState and Config.Applied=1, so the applied<committed gap is produced by the application lag the field models.
Probe B's authority change is produced by a real peer campaigning over the in-process network, not by calling an internal transition.

experiment.prefix: Probe A initializes a voter through newRaft(newTestConfig(1,10,1,ms)) with ms holding entries 1..2 and HardState{Term:1,Commit:2}, then steps MsgHup, then a second identical node steps MsgTimeoutNow{From:3,Term:r.Term}, then raftLog.appliedTo(2,0) followed by MsgHup, plus a control node whose entry 2 is normal. Probe B elects a leader with MsgHup through newNetwork, commits one proposal, admits MsgReadIndex{Entries:[{Data:"A"}]} directly on the leader, then lets peer 2 campaign via the network, and finally admits MsgReadIndex{Data:"B"} on the new leader and steps one MsgHeartbeatResp carrying the context of the leader's own heartbeat.

result.summary: Built and ran the two registered probes in one fixed harness (draft/assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, reusing the repo's own test helpers) and recorded the outcomes, then requested formal execution of that same harness so the results rest on retained receipts instead of local feedback only. Campaign guard: a voter with entry 2 = EntryConfChangeV2, HardState.Commit=2 and Config.Applied=1 reports has_unapplied=true and stays StateFollower with 0 messages on both MsgHup and term-carrying MsgTimeoutNow; after raftLog.appliedTo(2,0) it campaigns (StateCandidate, term 2, MsgVote to voters [2,3]), and the control with a normal entry at index 2 and the same applied/committed gap campaigns immediately - so the suppression is keyed on the entry type in (applied, committed] and is transient, which refutes the stale-voter-set branch of that suspicion while leaving its bounded-liveness cost (a requested leadership transfer is refused until the application catches up) as the noted limit. ReadIndex: a leader that admits a read and then loses its term before any quorum ack drops that request with no completion (read_states=0, unconfirmed_reads=0), while a read admitted on the new leader is confirmed by one peer ack and delivered with an index equal to the commit index at admission - i.e. loss, not staleness, and that lossiness is already placed on the caller by the Node.ReadIndex contract. No defect is asserted for either question; both are recorded as source-explained negatives and the decisive readings (has_unapplied/applied/committed, vote targets, unconfirmed vs confirmed reads, ctx completions, read indices) are the operands a later interpretation will cite against the incoming CheckRun receipt. Still open: the receipt-backed successor interpretation, gap closures for both questions, and any independent sourced lead beyond these two mechanisms.
